Definition: probably from the same as G1171 (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange); so and so (when the person is not specified):--such a man.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, as a pronoun for a man whose name is left unsaid: such a man, in such a place, at such a time. It is the deliberate vagueness of a story that does not need the name.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word reminds us that Scripture names what matters and leaves the rest unnamed, and the unnamed still belong to God.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
